doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: Missing-middle and family-suitable housing, plus "housing of all kinds, especially deeply affordable." No unit target and no 25/20/15 composition shares.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: An authorized campaign site with a complete ten-part platform (housing, homelessness, safety, transportation, climate, business, arts, governance, reconciliation, miscellaneous) plus dated blogs. Written and current. No costed budget, no tax formula, no unit target, no implementation calendar.

cells.quote: The city should make it easier to build Missing Middle housing, so that nobody is forced to choose between living in Victoria and raising a family.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: missing middle and family-suitable forms named (townhomes, rowhomes, houseplexes, more bedrooms), plus the plank headline "housing of all kinds, especially deeply affordable." Not 25/20/15, no unit target. Same-plank mansion tax to fund non-market is this cluster, not a second mark. Feb 2026 REIT post on vacancy-as-mechanism is diagnosis, not a 5% target, and is not scored here.

cells.quote: The city should pilot a financing program for these co-op projects, and once successful, the provincial government can adopt it province-wide.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: co-op financing, not a land-bank acquisition fund or 99-year leasehold. Described as near revenue-neutral. Non-market fee exemption is scored on row 5, not here.

cells.quote: The city should introduce guaranteed response timelines, where the answer is an automatic yes if no response is received from the city by the deadline.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: a permit-time instrument with deemed approval, starting at "say, 8 months" and ratcheting down. No published 90-day-class benchmark and no AI pre-screening. Pattern-book stream is scored on row 4.

cells.quote: Building townhomes should not require a bespoke application process every single time.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: expand the provincial catalogue of pre-approved designs. Same job as a city pattern book, not the city's own duplex/triplex/townhome/laneway book. One cluster with the catalogue heading on the same plank.

cells.quote: The city should commit to not further raising taxes on new homebuyers and renters.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: freeze on new housing taxes/charges/fees, plus same-plank permanent exemption of non-market housing from all taxes, charges and fees, plus the 29 Jan 2026 blog's course "to a world without" DCCs. No 5% vacancy target and no suite amnesty. Backyard-suite "cumbersome" sits inside the missing-middle paragraph already used on row 1. One cluster.

cells.quote: Increase funding for CRCL and other non-police repsonse programs, to better respond to community members in crisis.
cells.why: Commits × Same instrument: CRCL named. Context, same plank: "not being overly reliant on police for everything" so police can "do actual police work." No dispatch criteria, no funding figure, no published diversion number. Typo "repsonse" is in the source.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)

cells.quote: We need to change our funding model to one which allows cities and regions to fund transit if they want to, and we need to advocate to the province for a significant increase in transit funding, both for day-to-day operations, as well as necessary capital expenditures like a new transit yard.
cells.why: Commits × Neither: a provincial-funding ask, no published ledger, no refusal threshold. Bus lanes and signal priority on the same transportation plank are scored on row 28, not here. Commercial-vacancy-tax advocacy is scored on row 18.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: We must advocate to the province for a commercial vacancy tax, to tip the scales in favor of actually using valuable downtown space instead of hoarding it for speculative purposes.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: downtown vacancy instrument, provincial ask rather than a City vacancy target, Strategic Economic Plan, or "one mandate not a new office." Same-plank home-based businesses, stacked industrial units, and hotels are this cluster, not second marks.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
cells.quote: This could include establishing regular meetings between Council and local Nation leadership, involving Indigenous representatives earlier in relevant planning processes, and seeking Indigenous input on major projects and policies.
cells.why: Commits to "more consistent opportunities" for Nations in City decisions × Comparable: a standing-meeting table, cultural-awareness training for councillors and staff, and enabling Songhees and Xʷsepsəm (Esquimalt) development of the Matullia lands in Rock Bay. Not the full Foundation package (procurement target, place-names programme, urban Indigenous liaison). "Could include" is noted; ambiguity resolves up from Partial+.

cells.what: tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: The city should strengthen the tenant protection bylaw, to encourage development of owner-occupied housing.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: expand the existing tenant-protection bylaw. Not STR licensing, not indoor heat. Same-cluster homelessness plank: change zoning so redevelopment is not concentrated where displacement is highest. One cluster. M9c struck — not scored.

cells.quote: Building on work by councillor Loughton and colleagues in Vancouver, we should hire a staff member whose job will be to ensure that people are helped along to the next stage as soon as they're ready, freeing up badly needed space for others.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: a STEP-like throughput instrument on the supportive-housing continuum. No Housing First name, no 50% unsheltered target, no quarterly count. Same-cluster rent-bank funding to "keep people housed" is prevention, not a second mark.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
cells.quote: We should build on their success and build our own municipally-run clinic.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: Colwood/Langford municipal-clinic model to attract family doctors. Childcare spaces and the 18–25 cohort are not named. School food is $0 and lives on M13d, next row. School-gym arts use is scored on row 39, not here.

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: Increase traffic enforcement, to keep our roads safe for everyone.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: traffic-enforcement as a road-safety instrument, plus same-plank "legalizing actually visible road paint" against "traffic violence." Not a Vision Zero audit, not M38 calming design. M39 30 km/h is struck — not scored. Bike Valets and extended hours are this mobility cluster, not a second mark. Bus lanes are row 28. Pedestrian streets are row 37.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
cells.quote: Building on the success of the Douglas street bus lanes, the city should expand our bus lane network on key transit corridors.
cells.why: Commits × Same instrument: City-controlled bus lanes, plus same-sentence cluster "every new traffic signal is equipped with signal priority infrastructure." Douglas Street rail preparation (City ROW ready for future rail) is this cluster, not a second mark. Provincial matching-fund advocacy is already scored on row 16. Sidewalk-gap standard is not stated.

cells.quote: Build more public washrooms, and better maintain the ones we already have, to keep our streets clean and improve accessibility.
cells.why: Commits × Same instrument: public bathrooms as walking infrastructure, city-wide, plus maintenance. No hours standard, no accessibility audit, no named location. Platform-summary accessible downtown parking is this cluster (accessibility), not M75, and is not a second mark. The full transportation plank does not repeat that parking bullet.

cells.what: VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: By regionalizing our police force, we can reduce costs, eliminate redundancies, and increase coordination for better results for everyone.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: a regional-policing instrument, not Esquimalt formula and not convene-and-publish. Stronger than a review; still the same goal as M29b. Feasibility FLAG in working notes: a councillor cannot bind another force — scored as published, not as Opposed. Not a defund. CRCL is row 7.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target

cells.quote: The city should explore every possible avenue to make the creation of new arts spaces as easy and low-cost as possible, removing unnecessary barriers and fees wherever possible.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: reuse/renovate old spaces as cultural venues. Not facade grants, not a venue lease-bridge, not a heritage HIA. Arts funding is scored on row 39. One sentence, one measure.

cells.quote: Explore new pedestrian streets where appropriate, to increase vibrancy and improve safety.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: pedestrianisation named, as exploration rather than a designated zone list. Context: Government Street pilot and Broad Street between Fort and Broughton as successes to extend. No signature-project shortlist, no referendum, nothing on M45c. Weaker than a "more pedestrian priority zones" delivery sentence; Close not Aligned.

cells.what: culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
cells.quote: Increase arts and culture funding, to keep our arts scene healthy and vibrant.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: an arts-funding increase, not a numbered floor, not sport. Same-cluster school-gym and underused-space activation for arts events. Venue-renovation barriers already on row 36.

cells.quote: Introduce a council voting dashboard, to increase transparency and make it easier to follow local politics.
cells.why: Commits × Neither: a named dashboard of who voted how, following Saanich, not quarterly city-wide KPIs and not a taxpayer capital portal. Distinct from the YouTube simulstream, which is M83-adjacent and has no cell.

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging

cells.quote: The city should do it's part to legalize these kits, and should advocate to the provincial and federal governments that they be legal for sale and installation in BC and across Canada.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: balcony / plug-in solar legalization as a municipal climate instrument. Not the 50%/2030 set, not district energy, not seismic. Same-plank cardboard recycling on construction sites, and "house more people near jobs" as emissions, are this cluster, not second marks. Housing supply itself is already scored on row 1. Typo "it's" is in the source.

cells.what: trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness
cells.quote: Increasing flexibility to allow for more greenspace and greater tree retention would ensure that we get the housing we need while continuing to increase our tree canopy, provide more functional greenspace, and decreasing impermeable surfaces.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: a canopy/greenspace instrument without 5,000 trees / 35%. Same-cluster community and boulevard gardens. Mode share is inside transportation already scored on rows 27–28. No emergency-preparedness position.

cells.quote: Councillors who own investment properties should be required to verbally disclose how many properties they own, and how much money those properties generate every month, before they make housing and land use decisions.
cells.why: Commits × Comparable: a conflict-disclosure integrity instrument, also to be published on the City website. Not the Integrity Commissioner office and not a 60-day consultation-response standard. Voting dashboard is row 42, not here.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
